ledger.note: 1588: Charles Emmanuel I occupies the Marquisate of Saluzzo. 'In the autumn of 1588, taking advantage of the civil war weakening France, he occupied the Marquisate of Saluzzo'; the Duchy of Savoy page calls it 'the territory of Saluzzo, previously ceded to France'. Savoy is the occupier here; France is the owner. Saluzzo is not in the gazetteer, so a 25 km disc round the town stands for the marquisate.
1601: the occupation of Saluzzo ends in a treaty. 'with the Treaty of Lyon (17 January 1601), Saluzzo went to Savoy in exchange for Bresse, Bugey, and Gex.'

1601: the Treaty of Lyon gives Saluzzo to Savoy. 'with the Treaty of Lyon (17 January 1601), Saluzzo went to Savoy in exchange for Bresse, Bugey, and Gex.' The Duchy of Savoy page: 'the territory of Saluzzo, previously ceded to France, in 1601 under the Treaty of Lyon'.

1601: the Treaty of Lyon takes Bresse, Bugey and Gex from Savoy. 'Saluzzo went to Savoy in exchange for Bresse, Bugey, and Gex.' The region is read as the Ain departement (Bresse, Bugey, Gex, 5,564 km2) against 19 cells (about 4,800 km2) that Cliopatria removes in 1602; the page does not mention Valromey.

March 1629: France takes Pinerolo. War of the Mantuan Succession page: 'by the end of the month, they had lifted the siege of Casale and taken the strategic Savoyard fortress of Pinerolo' (Louis XIII's march through the Pas de Suse in March 1629). The formal award to France is the Treaty of Cherasco (1631 entry below); the page also says Nevers and Victor Amadeus 'allowed French garrisons to remain in Casale and Pinerolo'. Month is the page's context (March 1629), not a dated sentence. Pinerolo is not in the gazetteer (12 km disc).

1630: France overruns Savoy. War of the Mantuan Succession page: 'A French army of 18,000 under Henri II de Montmorency overran Savoy, before invading Piedmont in February 1630'; the Duchy of Savoy infobox: 'Occupied by France: 1536-59, 1630, 1690-96, 1703-13'. The page gives no month for Savoy and no places for the Piedmontese campaign (Carignano 6 August 1630 is the only battle named), so the region is Savoy proper only. Charles Emmanuel I died on 26 July 1630 (Duchy of Savoy page). The earlier note that both pages were silent on 1630 was wrong: the Charles Emmanuel I page also has Richelieu ordering a French army into Savoy in 1630 (reviewer).

6 April 1631: the Treaty of Cherasco ends the war: 'All foreign troops are to be withdrawn' (a second agreement of 19 June 1631 confirmed it and 'added rules for withdrawing troops'). The page does not name France or Savoy in the withdrawal, so that the French left Savoy now is my reading of the clause.
6 April 1631: Pinerolo, held by France since March 1629, is 'awarded to France' by the Treaty of Cherasco, which turns the occupation into a cession (the loss entry that follows).

1631: the Treaty of Cherasco gives Savoy the Montferrat towns of Trino and Alba. 'The Montferrat towns of Trino and Alba were ceded to the Duke of Savoy' (6 April 1631, confirmed 19 June); Charles Emmanuel renounced his claims to Montferrat in return. The Cherasco page names only 'Montferrat'; the Charles Emmanuel I page ties Monferrato to Duke Francesco IV Gonzaga of Mantua, so the counterpart is the Gonzaga Duchy of Mantua (with Montferrat), which no row covers. The region is the five cells Cliopatria adds around the two towns in 1632.

region.text: the Montferrat towns of Trino and Alba and the cells Cliopatria adds around them in 1632

ledger.note: 1631: Pinerolo goes to France under the Treaty of Cherasco. 'the strategic Piedmontese location of Pinerolo' was 'awarded to France'; the page does not say from whom, the counterpart and the Savoyard holding are my reading. Pinerolo is not in the gazetteer (12 km disc).

1690: France occupies Savoyard lands in the Nine Years' War. Infobox: 'Occupied by France: 1536-59, 1630, 1690-96, 1703-13'. France is the occupier, Savoy the owner; the region is the 88 cells that Cliopatria leaves out of its 1691-1695 shape (Savoy, Nice and the western valleys). The page does not list the places or the month.

region.text: all Savoyard territories occupied by France

ledger.note: 1696: Pinerolo returns to Savoy after its fortifications are destroyed. Treaty of Turin, 29 August 1696: 'All Savoyard territories occupied by France would be returned, including Pinerolo'; the Victor Amadeus II page: 'the return of Pinerolo to Savoy'.

1703: France occupies Savoy again. Infobox: 'Occupied by France: ... 1703-13' (the Treaty of Turin (1696) page: 'occupied again between 1704 and 1714'). Savoy had switched sides: 'In 1703, Victor Amadeus switched sides, joining the Grand Alliance' (Victor Amadeus II page). The page names no places; Savoie and Haute-Savoie are the Savoyard heartland. The Siege of Turin page (reopened in the eu-13-j repair): French armies 'captured Savoyard territories north of the Alps in Villefranche and the County of Savoy' (1704), and the possessions north of the Alps 'were held by France until 1713'.

1703: France holds western Piedmont. The year is the Duchy of Savoy infobox's 'Occupied by France: ... 1703-13'. The Siege of Turin page (reopened in the eu-13-j repair): 'by the end of 1705 Turin was the only significant city still under Savoyard control' and 'By 1706, France occupied most of the Duchy of Savoy, with the exception of its capital Turin'; it names no Piedmontese town. The region is the cells Cliopatria drops in 1702-1705 apart from Savoy proper and, since the repair, apart from the County of Nice, whose occupation the County of Nice page dates to 1707-1713 (own entry below). Cliopatria drops the cells in 1702, a year before the infobox.

region.text: the Piedmontese cells Cliopatria drops from 1702 to 1705; Savoy and the County of Nice have their own entries

ledger.note: September 1706: the relief of Turin frees the Piedmontese lands. Siege of Turin page: 'The French were forced to withdraw from Northern Italy, allowing Victor Amadeus to recover most of Piedmont'; 'French garrisons in Pinerolo and Susa were withdrawn, and the forts reoccupied by Savoy' (no date on the page, placed after the 8 September action at Castiglione); the Victor Amadeus II page has 'Turin was saved by the combined forces of Victor Amadeus and Prince Eugene of Savoy in September 1706'. Savoy and the County of Nice stay occupied (own entries). Region as in the 1703 entry, without the County of Nice (eu-13-j repair).

region.text: the Piedmontese cells Cliopatria drops from 1702 to 1705; Savoy and the County of Nice have their own entries

ledger.note: 1707: France occupies the County of Nice. County of Nice page: 'the county was subjected to French occupation twice (1691-1697 and 1707-1713)'; the Siege of Turin page adds 'Nice and the County of Savoy were not returned by France until 1713'. The page is silent on 1705 and on the capture itself, and the Siege of Turin page has French armies taking 'Villefranche' in 1704, so the occupation may have begun earlier; 1707 is the County of Nice page's year and the one kingdom-of-france carries (its /ledger/153). Cliopatria drops the Nice cells in 1702; this dossier keeps them Savoyard and unhatched until 1707. Reviewer fix: Nice taken out of the 1703-1706 Piedmont occupation.

ledger.note: 1713: Victor Amadeus II receives the Kingdom of Sicily. 'At the end of the war in 1713, Victor Amadeus II received the Kingdom of Sicily'; infobox 'Acquired Sicily and parts of Duchy of Milan: 11 April 1713'. The Treaty of Utrecht page: Spain 'signed separate peace treaties with Savoy and Great Britain at Utrecht on 13 July'. The page does not name the ceding party; Spain held Sicily.

11 April 1713: parts of the Duchy of Milan pass to Savoy. Duchy of Savoy infobox 'Acquired Sicily and parts of Duchy of Milan: 11 April 1713'; Treaty of Utrecht: 'Savoy receiving Sicily and parts of the Duchy of Milan'. Alessandria page: 'In 1707 ... Alessandria was occupied by the imperial army' and 'the peace of Utrecht resulted in the annexation of Alessandria to the Duchy of Savoy'; Lomellina page: 'In 1707 ... a part of Lomellina was conquered by the Piedmontese House of Savoy' (so part of the land was held earlier). Duchy of Milan page: Austrian rule from 1707, hence habsburg-monarchy as the counterpart (Spain ceded Milan to Austria at Utrecht). No page opened names Valenza or Valsesia. The region is the 8 cells Cliopatria adds in 1713 beyond Sicily (lon 8.0-8.85 E, lat 44.9-45.9 N), a reading that covers Alessandria and Lomellina. Reviewer fix: the 1709 Montferrat cells are no longer here (see the 1708 entry); habsburg-monarchy has no matching loss (route to eu-09).

region.text: the Milanese districts (Alessandria, part of Lomellina) ceded in 1713: the 8 cells Cliopatria adds in 1713 beyond Sicily

ledger.note: 1713: Savoy gives the Ubaye Valley (Barcelonnette) to France. Barcelonnette page: 'reattached to France in 1713 as part of a territorial exchange with the Duchy of Savoy during the Treaties of Utrecht'; War of the Spanish Succession page: France 'was awarded the Principality of Orange and Ubaye Valley'; County of Nice page: the Ubaye passed to the Savoy domains in 1388. The page gives the year only; April is the date of the Utrecht settlement with Savoy (11 April 1713, Duchy of Savoy infobox) and matches kingdom-of-france /ledger/160. The region is a 15 km disc round Barcelonnette (3 cells), which Cliopatria draws as French before 1713 (see the keyframes). Reviewer fix: loss and exchange added.

1713: Savoy receives the Italian Dauphine in exchange. Dauphine page: the Italian Dauphine 'belonged to the Republic of the Escartons until 1713, when it was ceded to the Duchy of Savoy by the Treaty of Utrecht'; the province 'lost the major part of the Briançonnais'. The page names the Oulx valley, Pragelato and Casteldelfino only in a sentence on the dialect spoken there, and is silent on Exilles, Fenestrelle and Château-Dauphin; the discs are my placement. The counterpart is my reading (the Escartons lay in the French province of Dauphine); kingdom-of-france has no matching loss (route to eu-10). Cliopatria already draws cells here as Savoyard (4 of the 7 from 1564, all 7 from 1588), which the cell scale does not let me separate from Savoy's own Susa valley. Reviewer fix: gain added.

region.text: the Italian Dauphine: the Oulx valley, Pragelato (Upper Val Chisone) and Casteldelfino, beyond the Alpine watershed

ledger.note: 1718: Spain invades Sicily. 'In July 1718 the Spanish landed 30,000 men on Sicily.' Spain is the occupier, Savoy the owner; Cliopatria drops Sicily from the Savoyard shape here, the dossier keeps it hatched until the cession of 1720.
1719: Austrian forces retake Sicily from Spain. 'Austrian land forces later retook Sicily in October 1719.'
1719: Austria holds Sicily after retaking it. Austria 'retook Sicily in October 1719'; the page does not say whether it held it for Savoy or for itself pending the settlement.
1720: Austrian occupation of Sicily ends in the cession. Hague settlement, 17 February 1720.

1720: Savoy cedes Sicily to Austria. Infobox of the War of the Quadruple Alliance: 'Savoy cedes Sicily to Austria'; Philip V made peace with the allies 'with the Treaty of The Hague on 17 February 1720'; 'Victor Amadeus II reluctantly exchanged Sicily for Sardinia in 1720' (Duchy of Savoy page). Savoy rule over Sicily lasted 'seven years (1713-1720)' (House of Savoy page). The handover date is not on the page.

1720: Austria cedes Sardinia to Savoy. Infobox: 'Austria cedes Sardinia to Savoy'; Spain had landed on the island in August 1717 and 'by November had re-established control' (Spain's hold ended in the same settlement; the page gives no date).

1720: the Duchy of Savoy becomes the Kingdom of Sardinia. The House of Savoy page lists 'King of Sicily (1713-1720)' and 'King of Sardinia (1720-1861)': the same Savoyard state under the new royal title, which Cliopatria carries as a separate row from 1721 (kingdom-of-sardinia).

region.text: the Savoyard mainland and the island of Sardinia, passed to the Kingdom of Sardinia

wars.name: First Monferrato war

zones.text: Monferrato (the page names the district, not the lands)

wars.outcome: Ended with a compromise signed in Paris and Madrid in September 1617; the page records no change of frontier.
wars.note: The page gives the trigger ('on the death in 1612 of Duke Francesco IV Gonzaga of Mantua') and the compromise ('September 1617'), not the first campaign; 1612 is the page's year.

wars.name: War of the Mantuan Succession

zones.text: the Montferrat towns of Trino and Alba

wars.outcome: Treaty of Cherasco, 6 April 1631 (confirmed 19 June): Trino and Alba to Savoy, Savoy renounces other claims to Montferrat, Pinerolo awarded to France.
wars.note: 'When the French occupied Casale Monferrato during the War of the Mantuan Succession in 1628, Charles Emmanuel allied again with Spain' (Charles Emmanuel I page); Savoy was also invaded in 1630 (infobox 'Occupied by France: ... 1630', no land named). Belligerent lists beyond the Cherasco signatories (France, the Empire, Savoy, with Spain and the Pope present) are not on the page. Repair: France took Pinerolo in March 1629 and overran Savoy before invading Piedmont in February 1630 (War of the Mantuan Succession page; occupation entries 1629, 1630 and 1631 in the ledger); the page dates the Treaty of Cherasco to 19 June 1631, the Treaty of Cherasco page to 6 April and 19 June 1631.

wars.name: Nine Years' War (Savoyard front)

zones.text: the Savoyard territories occupied by France 1690-96

wars.outcome: Savoy made a separate peace with France in the Treaty of Turin (29 August 1696): all occupied territories returned, including Pinerolo; the Convention of Vigevano (7 October 1696) set a general ceasefire in Italy.
wars.note: The page gives no start for the Savoyard fighting; 1690 is the first year of the infobox's occupation of the duchy. Staffarda and Marsaglia are not on the pages opened.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Savoyard front)

zones.text: the Piedmontese cells Cliopatria drops from 1702 to 1705; Savoy and the County of Nice have their own entries
'the county was subjected to French occupation twice (1691-1697 and 1707-1713)'
Montferrat (Casale Monferrato, Acqui): the 7 cells Cliopatria adds in 1709 (lon 8.1-8.6 E, lat 44.3-45.3 N)

wars.outcome: Turin relieved in September 1706; Montferrat passed to Savoy in 1708; at Utrecht in 1713 Savoy received Sicily and parts of the Duchy of Milan (11 April 1713) and the Dauphine valleys beyond the Alps, gave the Ubaye Valley to France, and France gave back Savoy and Nice.
wars.note: Victor Amadeus 'switched sides' in 1703. The war began in 1701; that year is not on the pages opened, so the Savoyard span starts with the switch. The truce between France and Savoy was 14 March 1713, Spain's separate peace with Savoy 13 July 1713 (Treaty of Utrecht page).

wars.name: War of the Quadruple Alliance

zones.text: Sicily, landed in July 1718, retaken by Austria in October 1719

wars.outcome: Treaty of The Hague, 17 February 1720: Savoy cedes Sicily to Austria and receives Sardinia.
wars.note: Savoy was on the allied side only in the settlement as far as the page shows; its part in the fighting is not on the page.

certainty.note: The restored duchy's extent is bridged from Cliopatria; no page opened gives the Alpine or Lake Geneva frontiers or the places held by foreign garrisons.

Frontiers fixed by dated treaties: Lyon (17 January 1601), Cherasco (6 April 1631), Turin (29 August 1696), Utrecht (11 April 1713) and The Hague (17 February 1720). The Alpine watershed and the Milanese border cells are Cliopatria's lines, approximate at cell scale.

notes:
Cliopatria's House of Savoy row (1564-1720) is the Duchy of Savoy, the same state as the County of Savoy row (to 1539, other group) and the Kingdom of Sardinia row (from 1721, kingdom-of-sardinia). This dossier starts in 1559, the Peace of Cateau-Cambresis, not 1564, with a new bridged keyframe 1559-1563; it ends in February 1720 with the Hague settlement, although Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sardinia row starts in 1721.
Page budget (9) was spent by the author; the eu-13-j repair of 2026-10-25 opened 10 more pages because the reviewer's fixes needed them (Duchy of Montferrat, Duchy of Milan, War of the Spanish Succession, County of Nice, Barcelonnette, Dauphine, Alessandria, Lomellina, Siege of Turin, War of the Mantuan Succession, plus Treaty of Cherasco and Duchy of Savoy reopened). Pages that said nothing: Treaty of Lausanne (1564) does not exist as a Wikipedia article (url_not_found); Emmanuel Philibert and House of Savoy are silent on 1564-1569. Still unverified: shapes 1564, 1572, 1595, 1642 and 1645 (one- to ten-cell changes; the Duchy of Savoy page, reopened, is silent on 1595 and 1642-1648), the Alpine valleys inside the 1588 shape, the extent of the 1559-1563 duchy. The civil war of 1639-42 is on the Duchy of Savoy page only as the looting of Turin on 27 July 1639 and 'Only in 1642 did the two factions reach an agreement'; it has no territorial effect on the pages and is not listed as a war.
Eu-13-j repair of 2026-10-25 (reviewer's findings): (1) the Lake Geneva restitution is 1564 (Republic of Geneva page; reviewer's edit), and the 1564 keyframe now carries the Geneva cells; (2) Montferrat passed to Savoy in 1708 (Duchy of Montferrat page), so the 1709 shape is right a year late and the 7 cells are a 1708 gain from duchy-of-mantua; the Milanese land of 11 April 1713 is the 8 cells Cliopatria adds in 1713 beyond Sicily (Alessandria page: annexed at Utrecht; Lomellina page: part conquered in 1707), counterpart habsburg-monarchy; (3) the County of Nice is occupied 1707-1713 (County of Nice page, as in kingdom-of-france /ledger/153 and 157), so the 1703-1706 Piedmont occupation no longer contains Nice (the Siege of Turin page puts French captures of Villefranche in 1704, so the true start may be earlier); (4) 1713: the Ubaye Valley goes to France (Barcelonnette page) and the Italian Dauphine (Oulx, Pragelato, Casteldelfino) comes to Savoy (Dauphine page; the page is silent on Exilles and Fenestrelle); (5) the French occupation of 1630 (War of the Mantuan Succession page) and the French hold on Pinerolo from March 1629 are added.
Disagreements with the reviewer: (a) the reviewer proposed 1705 as the start of the Nice occupation; the County of Nice page (the page both dossiers cite) gives 1707 and is silent on 1705, so 1707 is used; (b) the reviewer asked for verdict ok on the 1709 shape; I agree on Montferrat, but the shape is 'adjust' because the Ubaye cells are missing from it and from every pre-1713 Savoy shape (Cliopatria has them in France's shapes); (c) the Ubaye is a 3-cell, 15 km disc round Barcelonnette, not the 25 km disc that kingdom-of-france /ledger/160 uses, which reaches Savoyard Nice-county cells.
For other batches: kingdom-of-france (eu-10) has no mirror for the 1588-1601 Saluzzo occupation, the 1629-1631 Pinerolo and 1630 Savoy occupations, the 1631 Pinerolo gain, a Pinerolo loss in 1696, or the 1713 Dauphine loss, and its shapes carry the Ubaye cells before 1713; habsburg-monarchy (eu-09) has no 1713 loss of the Milanese districts to Savoy and no 1719 occupation of Sicily; kingdom-of-spain and habsburg-monarchy disagree on Sardinia 1718-1720.
Choices that a reviewer may want to revisit: (1) occupation is treated as occupation, not loss, so the 1691, 1702 and 1718 keyframes are 'adjust' and keep the occupied land in the shape; (2) 1572, 1588 and 1631 regions are Cliopatria cell differences or coordinate discs where the gazetteer lacks Saluzzo, Pinerolo, Alba, Trino and Chambery; (3) the 7 Italian Dauphine cells stay in the pre-1713 shapes because the cell scale cannot separate them from Savoy's own Susa valley.
Counterparts that need a dossier: duchy-of-mantua (Gonzaga Duchy of Mantua and Montferrat, 1612-1708; eu-13-x per the group scope). Disagreement between pages: French occupation of the transalpine lands 1703-13 (Duchy of Savoy infobox) against 1704-14 (Treaty of Turin (1696) page); Treaty of Cherasco 6 April 1631 (Treaty of Cherasco page) against 19 June 1631 (War of the Mantuan Succession page; the first page has both dates).
